topic: Hip replacement: what the first 12 weeks look like

slides.headline: Life after hip replacement, week by week
slides.sub: Every surgeon's protocol differs. This is a general picture, not your plan.

slides.title: Weeks 1 to 2: getting moving
slides.body: Most people are up and walking with an aid soon after surgery. Short, frequent walks, the exercises from the hospital team and following your surgeon's precautions are the main jobs.

slides.title: Weeks 2 to 6: building routine
slides.body: Walking distance usually grows, and exercises often progress towards more standing strength and balance work. Swelling and tiredness are common. Your surgeon's advice on movement limits and driving comes first.

slides.title: Weeks 6 to 12: getting stronger
slides.body: Many people rely less on walking aids and build hip and leg strength more steadily. Stairs, longer walks and everyday tasks often feel easier, though progress varies a lot between people.

slides.title: Everyone's timeline differs
slides.body: Age, fitness before surgery, other health conditions and the surgical approach all affect recovery. Comparing yourself with a friend or neighbour rarely helps. Steady, gradual progress is the aim.

slides.title: When to call your surgeon or GP
slides.body: Increasing redness, warmth or discharge around the wound, fever, new calf pain or swelling, or a sudden change in how the hip feels need prompt medical advice. Chest pain or breathlessness needs urgent care.

caption:
Hip replacement coming up, or just home from hospital? Here's a rough picture of the early months.

The first couple of weeks are mostly about short, frequent walks and the exercises from your hospital team. After that, strength and balance work usually builds, and many people gradually rely less on walking aids.

Everyone's timeline is different. Your fitness before surgery, other health conditions and the surgical approach all play a part, and your surgeon's protocol always comes first.

Wound changes, fever or new calf swelling need prompt medical advice.
